items.wrong: The life is difficult for students.
items.right: Life is difficult for students.

why.ar: في العربية نقول «الحياة» و«التعليم» بأل التعريف، لكن الإنجليزية لا تستخدم the مع الأسماء المجردة أو العامة.
why.en: English uses no article with abstract or general nouns.

detect.re: \bthe (life|education|society|technology|nature|money|health|happiness|success|time|pollution|unemployment|people in general)\b(?! of| in| that| which| we| they| at)

msg.ar: غالبًا لا تحتاج «the» هنا لأن الاسم عام.
msg.en: You probably don’t need “the” with this general noun.

drill.s: The education is the key to success.
drill.a: Education is the key to success.

drill.s: The technology has changed our lives.
drill.a: Technology has changed our lives.

drill.s: Many people believe that the money brings happiness.
drill.a: Many people believe that money brings happiness.

drill.s: The pollution is a serious problem.
drill.a: Pollution is a serious problem.

items.wrong: This problem very serious.
items.right: This problem is very serious.

why.ar: الجملة الاسمية العربية لا تحتاج فعلًا («المشكلة خطيرة»)، أما الإنجليزية فتحتاج is/are/was.
why.en: English sentences need a verb; use is/are/was before adjectives.

msg.en: The verb “to be” (is/are) seems to be missing.

drill.s: Children very curious.
drill.a: Children are very curious.

drill.s: The city so crowded in summer.
drill.a: The city is so crowded in summer.

drill.s: These solutions really useful.
drill.a: These solutions are really useful.

drill.s: My brother too busy to help.
drill.a: My brother is too busy to help.

items.wrong: The number of cars have increased.
items.right: The number of cars has increased.

why.ar: الفعل يطابق الفاعل الحقيقي (The number) وليس الكلمة الأقرب (cars).
why.en: The verb agrees with the real subject (“the number”), not the nearest noun.

msg.en: The subject is singular, so use has/is/was.

drill.s: The amount of waste are growing.
drill.a: The amount of waste is growing.

drill.s: Many people is unhappy with the service.
drill.a: Many people are unhappy with the service.

drill.s: Every student have a laptop.
drill.a: Every student has a laptop.

drill.s: The percentage of women in work have risen.
drill.a: The percentage of women in work has risen.

items.wrong: Cars are expensive, many people use buses.
items.right: Cars are expensive, so many people use buses.

why.ar: في العربية نصل الجمل بالواو والفواصل بحرية. في الإنجليزية لا تربط جملتين كاملتين بفاصلة فقط؛ استخدم نقطة أو أداة ربط (so, but, because).
why.en: Two full sentences cannot be joined by a comma alone; use a full stop or a linking word.

drill.s: I like this city, it is very clean.
drill.a: I like this city because it is very clean.

drill.s: The test was difficult, I passed it.
drill.a: The test was difficult, but I passed it.

drill.s: Prices are rising, people are spending less.
drill.a: Prices are rising, so people are spending less.

items.wrong: Technology is useful and it saves time and it helps students and it is cheap.
items.right: Technology is useful because it saves time. Moreover, it helps students and is relatively cheap.

why.ar: الواو العربية تربط كل شيء، لكن تكرار and في الإنجليزية يضعف درجة التماسك. نوّع: moreover, because, however, which.
why.en: Repeating “and” lowers Coherence and Cohesion; vary your linking.

msg.ar: استخدمت «and» ثلاث مرات في جملة واحدة. قسّم الجملة أو نوّع أدوات الربط.
msg.en: “and” three times in one sentence: split it or vary your linkers.

drill.s: The city is big and it is noisy and it is expensive.
drill.a: The city is big, noisy and expensive.

drill.s: I study and I work and I have no free time.
drill.a: Because I both study and work, I have no free time.

drill.s: He is clever and he is kind and everyone likes him.
drill.a: He is clever and kind, so everyone likes him.

items.wrong: I am interested about science.
items.right: I am interested in science.

why.ar: حروف الجر تُحفظ مع الكلمة ولا تُترجم من العربية: interested in، depend on، good at، married to.
why.en: Learn prepositions with their words; don’t translate them.

drill.s: It depends of the weather.
drill.a: It depends on the weather.

drill.s: She is good in mathematics.
drill.a: She is good at mathematics.

drill.s: We discussed about the problem.
drill.a: We discussed the problem.

drill.s: The team consists from five people.
drill.a: The team consists of five people.

items.wrong: The goverment should invest in enviroment protection.
items.right: The government should invest in environmental protection.

why.ar: كلمات يخطئ فيها كثيرون لأن بعض الحروف لا تُنطق بوضوح.
why.en: Silent or unclear letters cause frequent errors.

drill.s: I beleive this is true.
drill.a: I believe this is true.

drill.s: Students need cheap accomodation.
drill.a: Students need cheap accommodation.

drill.s: This is necesary for sucess.
drill.a: This is necessary for success.

items.wrong: My brother he works in a bank.
items.right: My brother works in a bank.

why.ar: لا تكرر الفاعل بضمير بعده مباشرة.
why.en: Do not repeat the subject with a pronoun.

msg.en: Don’t repeat the subject with a pronoun.

drill.s: The government it should help.
drill.a: The government should help.

drill.s: My friend she lives in Dubai.
drill.a: My friend lives in Dubai.

drill.s: The teacher he explained it again.
drill.a: The teacher explained it again.

items.wrong: This is the book which I bought it yesterday.
items.right: This is the book which I bought yesterday.

why.ar: في العربية: «الكتاب الذي اشتريته» (الهاء تعود على الكتاب). في الإنجليزية which/that تغني عن الضمير.
why.en: After “which/that”, don’t add “it/them”.

drill.s: The city that I visited it was beautiful.
drill.a: The city that I visited was beautiful.

drill.s: These are the problems which we discussed them.
drill.a: These are the problems which we discussed.

drill.s: The car which he bought it is red.
drill.a: The car which he bought is red.

items.wrong: We need more informations and advices.
items.right: We need more information and advice.

why.ar: information, advice, equipment, research, furniture, homework لا تُجمع.
why.en: These nouns have no plural form.

msg.ar: هذا الاسم غير معدود ولا يُجمع.

drill.s: The teacher gave us many homeworks.
drill.a: The teacher gave us a lot of homework.

drill.s: They bought new furnitures.
drill.a: They bought new furniture.

drill.s: Can you give me some advices?
drill.a: Can you give me some advice?

items.wrong: Students must make their homework.
items.right: Students must do their homework.

why.ar: العربية تستخدم «يعمل/يفعل» لكل شيء. الإنجليزية: do homework، make a decision، take an exam.
why.en: Learn the collocations: do homework, make a decision, take an exam.

msg.ar: الصحيح: make a decision / make a mistake.

drill.s: He did a big mistake.
drill.a: He made a big mistake.

drill.s: I will make the exam next week.
drill.a: I will take the exam next week.

drill.s: The manager did a decision.
drill.a: The manager made a decision.

items.wrong: Kids are gonna use phones a lot.
items.right: Children are likely to use phones frequently.

why.ar: تجنب في المقالة: kids, gonna, wanna, stuff, a lot of, can’t, don’t. استخدم لغة أكاديمية.
why.en: Avoid informal words and contractions in Task 2.

msg.ar: كلمة غير رسمية؛ استخدم بديلًا أكاديميًا.
msg.en: Informal word: use a formal alternative.

drill.s: Lots of kids don't do sports.
drill.a: Many children do not do any sport.

drill.s: This stuff is really bad for health.
drill.a: These products are very harmful to health.

drill.s: It's gonna be a big problem.
drill.a: It is likely to become a serious problem.

items.wrong: All young people are addicted to phones.
items.right: Many young people spend too much time on their phones.

why.ar: التعميم المطلق (all, always, never, everyone) يضعف حجتك. استخدم many, most, tend to, often.
why.en: Absolute claims weaken arguments; hedge them.

msg.ar: تعميم مطلق؛ خففه بـ many أو often أو tend to.
msg.en: Absolute claim: hedge with many/often/tend to.

drill.s: Everyone knows that fast food is bad.
drill.a: It is widely accepted that fast food is unhealthy.

drill.s: Students never read books now.
drill.a: Students tend to read fewer books now.

drill.s: All parents want the best for their children.
drill.a: Most parents want the best for their children.

items.wrong: It is very importance to study.
items.right: It is very important to study.

why.ar: انتبه: important (صفة) / importance (اسم)؛ benefit/beneficial؛ success/successful.
why.en: Use the correct part of speech.

msg.ar: بعد very تحتاج صفة (important, successful, dangerous…).

drill.s: Exercise is very benefit for health.
drill.a: Exercise is very beneficial for health.

drill.s: He was very success in business.
drill.a: He was very successful in business.

drill.s: We must understand the important of sleep.
drill.a: We must understand the importance of sleep.

items.wrong: In 2000, the number increase to 50%.
items.right: In 2000, the number increased to 50%.

why.ar: وصف بيانات سنوات ماضية يكون بالماضي البسيط (increased, fell)، والتوقعات بـ is expected to / will.
why.en: Use the past simple for past data, and “is expected to” for projections.

msg.en: Past date: use the past simple.

drill.s: In 1990, sales rise sharply.
drill.a: In 1990, sales rose sharply.

drill.s: By 2010, the figure fall to 20%.
drill.a: By 2010, the figure had fallen to 20%.

drill.s: In 2030, the population will reaches 10 million.
drill.a: In 2030, the population is expected to reach 10 million.

items.wrong: in saudi arabia, people speak arabic.
items.right: In Saudi Arabia, people speak Arabic.

why.ar: العربية بلا حروف كبيرة، لكن الإنجليزية تتطلبها في بداية الجملة وأسماء البلدان واللغات والأيام وضمير I.
why.en: Capitalise sentence starts, countries, languages, days and “I”.

msg.en: Start the sentence with a capital letter.

msg.ar: أسماء الأماكن واللغات والأيام تبدأ بحرف كبير.
msg.en: Proper nouns need a capital letter.

drill.s: i live in riyadh.
drill.a: I live in Riyadh.

drill.s: we study english on monday.
drill.a: We study English on Monday.

drill.s: my friend speaks arabic and french.
drill.a: My friend speaks Arabic and French.

items.wrong: Despite it was raining, we went out.
items.right: Although it was raining, we went out.

why.ar: despite + اسم أو -ing؛ although + جملة كاملة.
why.en: “Despite” + noun/-ing; “although” + clause.

msg.ar: بعد despite لا تأتي جملة كاملة؛ استخدم although أو despite the fact that.

drill.s: Despite he was tired, he finished.
drill.a: Although he was tired, he finished.

drill.s: Although the rain, we played.
drill.a: Despite the rain, we played.

drill.s: Despite it is expensive, people buy it.
drill.a: Although it is expensive, people buy it.

items.wrong: Many peoples think that…
items.right: Many people think that…

why.ar: people جمع person. «peoples» تعني الشعوب فقط.
why.en: “People” is already plural.

msg.ar: people جمع بالفعل؛ لا تضف s.

drill.s: Some peoples prefer to live alone.
drill.a: Some people prefer to live alone.

drill.s: Peoples in my city are friendly.
drill.a: People in my city are friendly.

drill.s: Many peoples believe this.
drill.a: Many people believe this.

items.wrong: In my opinion, I think that…
items.right: In my view, …

why.ar: «In my opinion, I think» تكرار. اختر واحدة، ونوّع: I would argue that، I firmly believe that.
why.en: “In my opinion, I think” is redundant.

msg.ar: تكرار: احذف I think أو In my opinion.
عبارة مقبولة لكنها مستهلكة؛ جرّب I would argue that.

drill.s: In my opinion, I believe it is wrong.
drill.a: I believe it is wrong.

drill.s: In my point of view, it is good.
drill.a: In my view, it is beneficial.

drill.s: From my point of view, I think that cities are too crowded.
drill.a: I would argue that cities are too crowded.

items.wrong: There are many advantage and two main reason.
items.right: There are many advantages and two main reasons.

why.ar: بعد many/several/two/few يأتي الاسم جمعًا دائمًا (في العربية التمييز قد يكون مفردًا).
why.en: After many/two/several, use a plural noun.

msg.ar: بعد هذه الكلمة يأتي الاسم جمعًا.
msg.en: Use the plural after this word.

drill.s: He lived there for three year.
drill.a: He lived there for three years.

drill.s: There are several solution.
drill.a: There are several solutions.

drill.s: Many student work part-time.
drill.a: Many students work part-time.
